clue.text: Forbid member supporting plucky player

parts.note: to forbid is to ban
a joist is a beam, a structural member that supports a floor or ceiling

explanation.surface: Someone tries to bar a club member who backs a brave performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plucky' looks like brave, but the player plucks strings.
explanation.definitionFit: A banjo is plucked, so its player is a plucky player in the literal sense of plucking strings.

clue.text: Article supporting a number of nationalists about a hateful thing

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below, so the article comes last
the anthem goes round the single letter a, holding it inside

parts.note: a national anthem is a number, a song, that nationalists sing
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper article backs a group of nationalists over something loathsome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A number' means a song, not a count: the national song. 'About' puts the second 'a' inside it, and 'supporting' puts the article A underneath, at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Something accursed or detested by everyone is a hateful thing; the word also means a formal curse.

clue.text: Dishonestly take a position as head waiter

definitions.meaning: to push in unfairly ahead of others waiting in line
read literally, one who leaps over everyone waiting ends up the first waiter in the line

explanation.walkthrough: 'Head waiter' looks like a restaurant title, but it is the person first in a line of people waiting.
explanation.definitionFit: Pushing in ahead of others in a line is taking a place in it unfairly, which makes you its foremost waiting person.

clue.text: Gang overwhelmed by savage fine for trespass

indicators.note: the gang is swamped by, so enclosed within, the scrambled letters around it
savage as a verb means to maul, so the letters of fine are torn into a new order

parts.note: a ring is a gang, as in a drugs ring

explanation.surface: A criminal gang is crushed by a stiff penalty for breaking the law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Savage' turns FINE into INFE, which holds RING to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To encroach on or break a right or rule is to trespass on it, both verbs meaning overstep.

clue.text: Become successful in satire

definitions.meaning: to start succeeding rapidly, as sales or a career might
a mocking imitation or parody of someone

explanation.surface: Someone makes their name by writing satire.
explanation.definitionFit: A rising career is said to soar like an aircraft leaving the runway, and a parody of a person is a mimicking send-up.

clue.text: Hoggish male going about ninety in US vehicle

indicators.note: the boar goes round, enclosing the Roman numeral

parts.note: a boar is a male pig
XC is ninety in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A greedy man drives round at ninety in an American car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hoggish' looks like greedy, but it means of a hog, a pig.
explanation.definitionFit: In American railroad usage this is an enclosed freight wagon, a vehicle on the rails.

clue.text: Learner in class used to make pottery

indicators.note: the learner's letter goes inside the word for class

parts.note: kin is a kind or class, as in 'of the same kin'
L is a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A beginner in a ceramics class is shown how pots are made.
explanation.definitionFit: Pots are fired in this oven, so it is the equipment used to make pottery.

clue.text: Sort found carrying drug allowed to send message

indicators.note: the word for sort holds the other pieces within it

parts.note: a type is a sort or kind
E is ecstasy
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A drug courier is found and allowed to send word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carrying' looks like smuggling, but it is the container signal: the sort word holds the drug and 'allowed' after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A teleprinter transmits typed text down a line, and the word also serves as the verb for sending by one.

clue.text: Such parents had no conception of the issue involved

definitions.text: Such parents had no conception of the issue involved

parts.words: Such parents had no conception of the issue involved
parts.note: 'conception' and 'issue' mean conceiving and offspring: these parents did not conceive the child they raise

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests parents who failed to understand a problem; 'issue' is a child and 'conception' its begetting.
explanation.definitionFit: Parents who take on someone else's child by legal process did not conceive that child.

clue.text: Mulled cordial

definitions.meaning: mulled wine is heated with spices
friendly and hearty, as a welcome might be

explanation.definitionFit: Mulled wine is served heated, and a cordial greeting is a friendly, heartfelt one.

clue.text: Deal with cash, after split with former partner

indicators.note: the cash comes after the other two pieces

parts.note: to part is to split
an ex is a former partner
change is cash in coins

explanation.surface: Someone settles up in cash after breaking up with an old partner.
explanation.definitionFit: A transaction where an old item is handed over as part payment for a new one is a kind of deal.

clue.text: Words of praise reviewing car magazine — good inside

indicators.note: the abbreviation for good goes within the rearranged letters
reviewing as re-viewing means the letters are looked at again in a new order

parts.note: G is good

explanation.surface: A motoring magazine reviews a car with glowing words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reviewing' shuffles CAR MAGAZINE, and 'inside' puts G among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The well-known hymn is sung to praise God, so its text is words of praise.

clue.text: Write about a male and a female bird

indicators.note: the word for write goes round the other pieces

parts.note: to pen is to write
he is a male

explanation.surface: Someone writes about a man and a woman, a pair of lovebirds.
explanation.definitionFit: The hen of a peafowl is the female of that showy bird.

clue.text: Dismiss a method to start making speech

parts.note: to fire is to dismiss from a job
a way is a method

explanation.surface: A boss sacks someone and finds a way to open the speech.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom invites someone to begin talking or asking questions, so it means start speaking.

clue.text: Some importing that French type of flooring

indicators.note: the word for some takes the French word into it

parts.note: part means some, as in 'part of it'
que is French for that

explanation.surface: Some French timber is imported for floors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' looks like a hidden-word signal, but it gives PART.
explanation.definitionFit: Wooden blocks laid in a geometric pattern make this floor covering.

clue.text: Almost fish around faulty power mains, perhaps

indicators.note: the shortened fish goes round the reworked letters
almost means the fish's word loses its final letter

parts.note: a pike is a fish

indicators.note: faulty says the letters of power are wrongly arranged

explanation.surface: A fish nearly swims round faulty electrical mains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Power mains' reads as one electrical phrase, but 'power' is anagram fodder (PEWOR, from 'faulty') and 'mains' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Water or gas mains are an example of a system of pipes, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Flow of quiz restricted by buzzer — two hands needed for it

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are held in by the buzzer's word

parts.note: a bee buzzes, so it is a buzzer

indicators.note: the letters of quiz flow into a new order

explanation.surface: A quiz show runs with buzzers, and contestants need both hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flow of' makes ZIQU. 'Buzzer' suggests a quiz-show button; it is an insect, and 'two hands' are hands of cards, not a contestant's.
explanation.definitionFit: This card game is played by two people, so two hands of cards are dealt for it.

clue.text: Type of ring suitable for all ages

definitions.meaning: a ring set with stones all round, symbolising endless love

explanation.surface: A jeweller recommends a style of ring that suits any age.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring with stones set right round its band is named for endless love, and endless time is every age.

clue.text: Mule thrashed with it comes round at last

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go round the word at
thrashed says the letters of mule and it are beaten into a new order

explanation.surface: A mule that was beaten finally comes round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thrashed' makes ULTIME, which 'comes round' the clue's 'at'. 'At last' looks like one phrase; only 'last' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Final means last in a series, and it also means the greatest.

clue.text: Queen, we hope, will be good enough for such tricks involving jack?

definitions.text: Queen, we hope, will be good enough for such tricks involving jack?

parts.words: Queen, we hope, will be good enough for such tricks involving jack?
parts.note: Britain's national hymn asks God to frustrate the enemies' rogue-like tricks; at cards, a queen beats a jack, which is also called a knave

explanation.walkthrough: The British national hymn, 'God Save the Queen', has the line 'Frustrate their ___ tricks'. At cards a queen outranks the jack, whose other name is knave, so a queen can beat tricks with a jack in them.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishonest, rascally tricks are the sort a scoundrel, or knave, plays.

clue.text: He was arrested as a juvenile

definitions.text: He was arrested as a juvenile

parts.words: He was arrested as a juvenile
parts.note: 'arrested' means stopped from growing up, not seized by police: J. M. Barrie's boy never grew older

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a young offender taken into custody; 'arrested' here is arrested development.
explanation.definitionFit: Barrie's hero is the boy who never grew up, his growth halted in childhood.

clue.text: Crude language from pickpocket pulled up short

indicators.note: in a down clue, pulled up means the word for pickpocket is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a dip is slang for a pickpocket
a short is a small measure of spirits, such as gin

explanation.surface: A pickpocket caught and stopped dead swears in coarse language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulled up short' reads as one phrase for stopping, but 'pulled up' turns DIP into PID and 'short' is a separate word for a drink: in Britain a short is a spirit, unlike beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough mixed tongue used for trade between speakers of different languages is a simplified, crude form of language.

clue.text: A fraction of some freight hauled

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Only part of a freight load was hauled.
explanation.definitionFit: One part in eight is a fraction, written as one over eight.

clue.text: I'd need a stick, I feel, to sort out lower stream!

definitions.text: I'd need a stick, I feel, to sort out lower stream!

parts.words: I'd need a stick, I feel, to sort out lower stream!
parts.note: a dowser walks with a forked stick, feeling for its twitch, to find water running underground

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower stream' is not a river's lower reaches but water below ground, and 'sort out' means locate; 'I feel' is literal, sensing the stick move.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowser searches for hidden underground springs with a hazel twig or rod.

clue.text: Underground TV

definitions.meaning: informal word for television, after the cathode-ray part inside old sets

explanation.definitionFit: Londoners call their underground railway by this nickname, and it is also slang for the television set.

clue.text: Just open a pint

parts.note: a jar is a pint of beer in British slang

explanation.surface: A pub has only just opened and someone orders a pint.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'jar' is British slang for a drink of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A door left slightly open is only just open.

clue.text: The men in this study are unnaturally well-built

definitions.text: The men in this study are unnaturally well-built

parts.words: The men in this study are unnaturally well-built
parts.note: the 'men' are machine men, mechanically constructed rather than born, and 'well-built' means skilfully manufactured, not muscular

explanation.walkthrough: 'Well-built' suggests muscular men; these men are literally built, as machines.
explanation.definitionFit: The discipline that designs and constructs automatons is the study of artificial mechanical men.

clue.text: Heavy ref stirred up perennial complaint

indicators.note: stirred up means the letters of heavy and ref are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A burly referee riles the crowd, who complain every season.
explanation.definitionFit: Pollen allergy returns every summer, so this ailment is a complaint that comes back year after year.
